subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for an alebrije design—a jaguar-eagle hybrid with quadruped body, hooked beak, feathered tail, and vibrant folk-art patterning like dots, stripes, and swirls, keeping the implementation compact but faithful to the SDK.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: hip joint positioned at the back, a spine chain curving up to the chest, and a neck chain extending forward and up to a head joint, sketching out approximate coordinates and segment names as I build out the rig.

For the eagle head itself, I'm planning a skull sphere with a hooked upper beak swept from a bezier curve, a lower beak on the jaw bone, oversized ringed eyes, and crest feathers extruding behind — painted in the bright, decorative alebrije style.

Now I'm thinking through coloring: turquoise head with a yellow beak, mostly flat colors with maybe some scattered dot decorations using small spheres in alternating hues along the body sweep for that alebrije texture. For the torso, I want to sweep a radius function along the spine chain starting from the hips joint, extending the path back to a rear starting point so the body has proper volume front to back.

I'm figuring out the body proportions — radius roughly 0.19-0.24 across the length, centered around y=0.68, with legs reaching from the belly down to the floor at y=0.05. I'm writing the radius function as a sine-based taper so it bulges in the middle like a chest and narrows at the ends, and now considering whether to color the body in distinct sectors or keep it uniform.

Now I'm working out the color scheme by region — orange sides, magenta back stripe, yellow belly — then planning jaguar rosette markings as small layered discs (turquoise ring, dark pink inner, yellow center dot) scattered across the coat, roughly 78 parts total for 26 rosettes. Next I'm setting up the four legs with inverted-kinematics style joints, starting with the front shoulder positions.

Still defining leg chain parameters...

The root joint with no parent is hips, with spine1 sharing that position as a child, and hind legs parent to hips. For side naming I'm using the sign of the x-offset to label left/right (positive x = left), building chain names like "hipL", then sweeping the leg radii through a tapering list of values along the chain.

I'm designing chunky paws using scaled spheres with small cone-shaped claws for a jaguar-eagle hybrid look, positioning the paw sphere just above ground level so it covers the leg tube's rounded end without clipping the floor.

Now I'm setting up the toe claws as spike primitives attached to the nearest leg bone, looping to place three per paw, then moving on to build the wing structure as a joint chain from shoulder through elbow and wrist to the wingtip, spreading outward and upward in an extended rest pose.

Adding alebrije color cycling and a contrasting inner stripe layer on each feather for extra depth, then setting up the along-path callback to extract frame points for placement.

I'm layering the wing with primary feathers (longer, 0.55/0.45) and a second row of shorter covert feathers (0.25) placed slightly offset in height and depth to avoid z-fighting while adding visual richness.

I'm checking the feather orientation math — cross product of the direction and up vectors — and realizing the current setup produces a vertical plane instead of the flat, horizontal feather shape I actually want, so I need to adjust the basis vectors.

Now I'm plotting the tail chain from hips to tip, curving upward and back to set up the eagle-feather fan at the end.

Still working out feather geometry...

Writing feather geometry helper...

Placing the head joint along the neck sweep and adding a feather collar at the neck base—a ring of feathers pointing outward and slightly downward to mimic the ruff of an eagle.

Using tangent crossed with outward to get the circumferential vector for feathers, with bone explicitly supplied each time. Feathers on the collar give it a ruffled identity with alternating colors, and now I'm sketching the skull as a scaled sphere positioned forward on the head bone.

Now I'm working out the eyes, brow ridges, and beak geometry: yellow eye spheres with black pupils offset outward-forward plus small white highlights, dark rod-shaped brow ridges angled above each eye, and an upper beak sweeping along a bezier curve from base to tip.

Placing small dark nostril spheres...

Now I'm leaving the mouth open with a lowered jaw, then thinking about adding small spot rosettes on the head using surface-based placement around the skull part, guarding against null hits. I'm also planning body decoration like a dorsal stripe or row of diamond shapes running along the spine, using the sweep/along functions on the body path.

Writing cone ridge details...

I'm also sketching out dot rows along the legs and cuff bands, and estimating total part counts to keep the geometry manageable—body, rosettes, ridge cones, legs, dots, paws, and claws.

Tallying up wings, tail, ruff, crest, and head bring me to roughly 320 triangles total, which feels fine for performance. I'm also considering extra decorative touches like a chest bib ellipsoid with dots and tiny flank stripe patterns to push the alebrije-painted look further.

Instead I'll settle on a chest medallion made of three concentric colored discs placed via a surface-hit normal projection, varying their radii and heights slightly for a layered rosette effect, and I'll mirror the same treatment on the hips as a rump medallion.

Adjusting the hind leg attachment x-offset outward slightly so the shoulders sit outside the body rather than inside it. For the wings, I'm anchoring the root near the upper spine inside the body silhouette, giving the wing chain four named joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand per side) with a tapered skin profile and a dedicated wing role for the skeleton structure.

Now I'm figuring out feather placement along the wing chain using the along helper, sampling points from the upper arm through the hand with feather length and outward spread increasing toward the tip, using the chain point's t value to interpolate direction and length, and loosely typing the callback parameter since the module's strictness is uncertain.

For the tail, I'm building a catmull-rom chain from the hips through four named segments curving up and back, then placing a fan of tail feathers at the terminal point, computing each feather's direction using an angle spread so the fan rises and spreads backward in a plausible arc.

Checking the floor contact: paws are the lowest points at y=0, with the foot spheres sized and positioned so they just touch the ground without sinking below it.

Now setting up the claw spikes along the base of the paw, keeping them close to the ground plane, and establishing the jaw joint hierarchy with a sweep for the lower beak curve.

I'm checking where the upper and lower beak surfaces meet so they overlap properly without gaps, then placing the skull sphere and its scale relative to the head joint, working out eye socket positions against the skull's curvature.

Now I'm setting up the neck geometry, figuring out its taper and how it connects into the skull sphere, and parenting the neck chain to the spine joint near the chest.

Defining more palette colors...

Still planning rosette placement and leg decorations...

Now I'm working out the ruff around the neck using two overlapping rings at different positions, each with its own radius, color, and outward-tilted feather direction computed from the neck's tangent and cross product.

Writing feather helper function...

Still defining feather geometry...

Now I'm thinking through head coloring instead - cream-white skull with gold beak, scattered small pink/turquoise dot rosettes at various azimuth/elevation positions around the head, plus a dark ring around the eye.

I'm adding an eye torus ring facing outward, decorative dots along the wing sweep, keeping the wings extended outward and slightly up with pink coloring, and skipping the tail fan base cap sphere. Time to write the code now.

Still writing joint chains...

Adding hind leg radii, deciding on leg dot sweeps, and setting up color cycling and RNG helpers for variation. I'm placing the chest medallion using spherical surface coordinates and adding dorsal cones embedded along the body's length.
